objects.definition:
typedef struct ZSTD_CCtx_s ZSTD_CCtx;
typedef ZSTD_CCtx ZSTD_CStream;  /**< CCtx and CStream are now effectively same object (>= v1.3.0) */
objects.description: Opaque compression context for Zstandard. ZSTD_CStream is an alias used for streaming compression; since v1.3.0 both denote the same underlying type.

objects.definition:
typedef struct ZSTD_DCtx_s ZSTD_DCtx;
typedef ZSTD_DCtx ZSTD_DStream;  /**< DCtx and DStream are now effectively same object (>= v1.3.0) */
objects.description: Opaque decompression context for Zstandard. ZSTD_DStream is an alias used for streaming decompression; since v1.3.0 both denote the same underlying type.
Opaque digested dictionary for compression. Can be shared across threads for repeated use.
Opaque digested dictionary for decompression. Can be reused to avoid per-call dictionary preparation.
By-value I/O struct describing an input buffer with a moving read position for streaming operations.
By-value I/O struct describing an output buffer with a moving write position for streaming operations.
Simple POD struct returned by parameter-bounds queries containing an error code and inclusive lower/upper bounds.

objects.definition:
typedef enum { ZSTD_fast=1,
               ZSTD_dfast=2,
               ZSTD_greedy=3,
               ZSTD_lazy=4,
               ZSTD_lazy2=5,
               ZSTD_btlazy2=6,
               ZSTD_btopt=7,
               ZSTD_btultra=8,
               ZSTD_btultra2=9
} ZSTD_strategy;
objects.description: Compression strategy selector from fastest to strongest; impacts search behavior and speed/ratio tradeoff.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
    ZSTD_c_compressionLevel=100,
    ZSTD_c_windowLog=101,
    ZSTD_c_hashLog=102,
    ZSTD_c_chainLog=103,
    ZSTD_c_searchLog=104,
    ZSTD_c_minMatch=105,
    ZSTD_c_targetLength=106,
    ZSTD_c_strategy=107,
    ZSTD_c_enableLongDistanceMatching=160,
    ZSTD_c_ldmHashLog=161,
    ZSTD_c_ldmMinMatch=162,
    ZSTD_c_ldmBucketSizeLog=163,
    ZSTD_c_ldmHashRateLog=164,
    ZSTD_c_contentSizeFlag=200,
    ZSTD_c_checksumFlag=201,
    ZSTD_c_dictIDFlag=202,
    ZSTD_c_nbWorkers=400,
    ZSTD_c_jobSize=401,
    ZSTD_c_overlapLog=402,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam1=500,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam2=10,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam3=1000,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam4=1001,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam5=1002,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam6=1003,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam7=1004,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam8=1005,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam9=1006,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam10=1007,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam11=1008,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam12=1009,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam13=1010,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam14=1011,
    ZSTD_c_experimentalParam15=1012
} ZSTD_cParameter;
objects.description: Selector enum for compression parameters set on a CCtx. Some values control LDM, frame flags, and multithreading; 500+ range are experimental toggles mapped to macros.
Controls scope of context reset for CCtx/DCtx: session state, parameters, or both.
Selector enum for decompression parameters set on a DCtx, including maximum window log and experimental toggles.
Streaming compression directive controlling whether to continue, flush, or end the current frame.

functions.name: ZSTD_versionNumber
functions.description: Returns the runtime Zstandard library version encoded as (MAJOR*100*100 + MINOR*100 + RELEASE). Useful for feature gating and diagnostics.

functions.name: ZSTD_versionString
functions.description: Returns the runtime Zstandard library version as a human-readable string like "1.5.2". Requires v1.3.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress(void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, int compressionLevel)
functions.description: Compresses the entire src buffer into a single ZSTD frame into dst. Faster if dstCapacity >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize). Returns compressed size or an error (check with ZSTD_isError()).
requirements: dst must point to a valid writable buffer of size >= dstCapacity.
src must point to readable memory of size >= srcSize.
dstCapacity must be large enough to hold the compressed output; hint: use ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize).
compressionLevel can be negative, 0 means default (ZSTD_CLEVEL_DEFAULT).
Return is a size or an error; caller must check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress(void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t compressedSize)
functions.description: Decompresses one or more concatenated ZSTD/skippable frames from src into dst. Returns number of bytes decompressed or an error (check with ZSTD_isError()).
requirements: compressedSize must be the exact size of a whole frame sequence (zstd/skippable).
dstCapacity must be an upper bound on the decompressed size; if unknown, prefer streaming.
dst must be a valid writable buffer; src must be a valid readable buffer.
Return is a size or an error; caller must check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_getFrameContentSize
functions.signature: unsigned long long ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: Reads a zstd frame header at src and returns the decompressed content size if known; otherwise returns ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN, or ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR on error. Requires src to point to frame start.
requirements: src must point to the start of a ZSTD frame.
srcSize must be >= the frame header size; any size >= ZSTD_frameHeaderSize_max is sufficient.
Return may be a 64-bit size and can be very large; caller must validate against application limits.
On untrusted input, the reported size may be incorrect; validate before allocating.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDecompressedSize
functions.signature: unsigned long long ZSTD_getDecompressedSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: Obsolete helper similar to ZSTD_getFrameContentSize() but conflates empty/unknown/error into 0. Returns decompressed size if known and non-empty, 0 otherwise.
requirements: Same input requirements as ZSTD_getFrameContentSize().
Prefer ZSTD_getFrameContentSize() for unambiguous results.

functions.name: ZSTD_findFrameCompressedSize
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_findFrameCompressedSize(const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: Given a buffer starting at a zstd or skippable frame, returns the exact compressed size of the first frame so it can be sliced/passed to ZSTD_decompress. Returns error on invalid input.
requirements: src must point to the start of a frame (zstd or skippable).
srcSize must be >= the full size of the first frame (i.e., buffer must contain the whole first frame).
Return is a size or an error; caller must check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_compressBound
functions.description: Returns a worst-case upper bound on compressed size for a single-pass compression of srcSize bytes. Useful to size dst buffers.
requirements: srcSize must be representable as size_t.

functions.name: ZSTD_isError
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the provided size_t is an error code returned by Zstd APIs, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: ZSTD_getErrorName
functions.description: Returns a human-readable error string corresponding to a Zstd error code, or a string for non-errors.

functions.name: ZSTD_minCLevel
functions.description: Returns the minimum (most negative) supported compression level. Requires v1.4.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_maxCLevel
functions.description: Returns the maximum supported compression level.

functions.name: ZSTD_defaultCLevel
functions.description: Returns the default compression level (ZSTD_CLEVEL_DEFAULT). Requires v1.5.0+.

functions.name: ZSTD_createCCtx
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new compression context. Reuse across compressions is recommended for performance.
requirements: Caller must free with ZSTD_freeCCtx().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCCtx
functions.description: Frees a compression context allocated by ZSTD_createCCtx(). Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: cctx may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressCCtx
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressCCtx(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, int compressionLevel)
functions.description: Same as ZSTD_compress(), but uses an explicit compression context. It compresses using only compressionLevel, ignoring other previously set parameters (they are reset).
requirements: cctx must be a valid created context.
dst/dstCapacity and src/srcSize must reference valid buffers; dst must be large enough to hold output (prefer ZSTD_compressBound).
compressionLevel semantics same as ZSTD_compress.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_createDCtx
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new decompression context. Reuse across decompressions is recommended.
requirements: Caller must free with ZSTD_freeDCtx().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDCtx
functions.description: Frees a decompression context allocated by ZSTD_createDCtx(). Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: dctx may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompressDCtx
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompressDCtx(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: Decompresses like ZSTD_decompress(), using an explicit DCtx. Compatible with sticky parameters set on the context.
requirements: dctx must be a valid created context.
src must contain exactly one or more complete frames and be readable for srcSize bytes.
dstCapacity must be an upper bound on decompressed size or use streaming if unknown.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_cParam_getBounds
functions.description: Returns bounds (inclusive) for a compression parameter, along with an error status field (test with ZSTD_isError()).
requirements: Caller must test returned bounds.error with ZSTD_isError() before using lowerBound/upperBound.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_setParameter(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, ZSTD_cParameter param, int value)
functions.description: Sets a single compression parameter on the CCtx. Parameters have valid bounds (see ZSTD_cParam_getBounds). Generally only possible before starting a frame; in multithreaded mode certain params may update mid-frame for future jobs.
requirements: cctx must be a valid context.
value must be within allowed bounds or it will be clamped or cause an error depending on parameter.
Most parameters must be set before starting compression; in MT mode only certain parameters can update during compression and affect subsequent jobs after a flush.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_setPledgedSrcSize
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_setPledgedSrcSize(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, unsigned long long pledgedSrcSize)
functions.description: Sets the total input size to be compressed as a single frame. Written into the frame header (unless disabled) and validated at end of frame. Overrides to srcSize when using one-shot APIs.
requirements: cctx must be valid.
pledgedSrcSize==ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN signals unknown size; 0 means an empty frame.
Value applies once for the next frame only and is then reset to unknown.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_reset
functions.description: Resets the compression context. You can reset just the session (abort current frame), just parameters (to defaults, clearing dictionary), or both. Parameter reset fails if compression is ongoing.
requirements: cctx must be valid.
Resetting the session never fails; resetting parameters is only allowed when no compression is active.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_compress2
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress2(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: One-shot compression using parameters previously pushed into cctx with the advanced API. Always starts a new frame and is blocking. Faster if dstCapacity >= ZSTD_compressBound(srcSize).
requirements: cctx must be configured via ZSTD_CCtx_set*() before call; any unfinished frame state is discarded.
dst must be a valid buffer of size >= dstCapacity; src must be readable for srcSize.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_dParam_getBounds
functions.description: Returns bounds (inclusive) for a decompression parameter, with an error status field (test with ZSTD_isError()).
requirements: Caller must test returned bounds.error with ZSTD_isError() before using lowerBound/upperBound.

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_setParameter
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_setParameter(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, ZSTD_dParameter param, int value)
functions.description: Sets a single decompression parameter on the DCtx. Parameters must be set before starting decompression of a frame.
requirements: dctx must be valid.
value must be within bounds or it will be clamped or error depending on parameter.
Parameters can only be set during frame initialization (before starting decompression).
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_reset
functions.description: Resets the decompression context’s session and/or parameters. Parameters can only be reset when no active frame is being decompressed.
requirements: dctx must be valid.
Parameters can only be reset when not actively decompressing a frame.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_createCStream
functions.description: Creates a streaming compression object (alias of CCtx).
requirements: Free with ZSTD_freeCStream().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCStream
functions.description: Frees a streaming compression object. Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: zcs may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream2
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressStream2(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input, ZSTD_EndDirective endOp)
functions.description: Streaming compression API with explicit end directive. Updates input->pos and output->pos. Returns a minimum number of bytes left to flush (>0 means more flushing needed) or 0 when fully flushed (for e_end/flush) or an error.
requirements: cctx must be configured via ZSTD_CCtx_set*().
input->pos <= input->size; output->pos <= output->size.
endOp must be a valid ZSTD_EndDirective.
With nbWorkers==0 the call is blocking; with nbWorkers>=1 it is non-blocking and guarantees forward progress.
If first call is ZSTD_e_end with sufficient dstCapacity it may delegate to ZSTD_compress2() (blocking).
Return non-zero indicates pending data to flush; caller must continue with ZSTD_e_flush/e_end until 0 for completion.
Check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_CStreamInSize
functions.description: Returns a softly recommended input buffer size for streaming compression.

functions.name: ZSTD_CStreamOutSize
functions.description: Returns a softly recommended output buffer size for streaming compression; large enough to flush at least one complete compressed block.

functions.name: ZSTD_initCStream
functions.description: Legacy helper to initialize a CStream with a compression level (resets session, clears dict, sets level). Returns 0 or hint/error. Kept for compatibility; new code should use reset + advanced API.
requirements: zcs must be a valid created CStream/CCtx.
Return value may be a hint or an error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compressStream(ZSTD_CStream* zcs, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input)
functions.description: Legacy streaming compression step. Updates positions. Returns a hint for next read size if >0, 0 when more input may be needed, or an error. Prefer ZSTD_compressStream2().
requirements: zcs must be initialized.
input->pos <= input->size; output->pos <= output->size.
Caller must loop until frame end using flush/end helpers.
Check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_flushStream
functions.description: Legacy helper equivalent to compressStream2(..., ZSTD_e_flush). Returns 0 when fully flushed, >0 when more flushes needed, or an error.
requirements: zcs must be initialized for streaming.
output->pos <= output->size.
Loop until return 0 to fully flush.
Check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_endStream
functions.description: Legacy helper equivalent to compressStream2(..., ZSTD_e_end). Returns 0 when frame is fully completed and flushed, >0 when more calls are needed, or an error.
requirements: zcs must be initialized for streaming.
output->pos <= output->size.
Loop until return 0 to finish the frame.
Check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_createDStream
functions.description: Creates a streaming decompression object (alias of DCtx).
requirements: Free with ZSTD_freeDStream().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDStream
functions.description: Frees a streaming decompression object. Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: zds may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_initDStream
functions.description: Legacy helper to initialize a DStream (resets session, clears dict). Returns the recommended first input size, or an error. Prefer advanced API for parameterized operation.
requirements: zds must be a valid created DStream/DCtx.
Return value >0 is a recommended next input size; check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_decompressStream
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompressStream(ZSTD_DStream* zds, ZSTD_outBuffer* output, ZSTD_inBuffer* input)
functions.description: Streaming decompression step. Updates positions. Returns 0 when a frame is fully decoded and flushed, >0 as a suggested next input size (more work to do), or an error.
requirements: zds must be initialized (e.g., via ZSTD_initDStream or advanced API).
input->pos <= input->size; output->pos <= output->size.
Caller must re-present unconsumed input until consumed and loop until 0 to finish frame.
Check errors with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_DStreamInSize
functions.description: Returns a softly recommended input buffer size for streaming decompression.

functions.name: ZSTD_DStreamOutSize
functions.description: Returns a softly recommended output buffer size for streaming decompression; guarantees flushing at least one complete block in all circumstances.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress_usingDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress_usingDict(ZSTD_CCtx* ctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const void* dict, size_t dictSize, int compressionLevel)
functions.description: One-shot compression at a specified level using a dictionary buffer (prefix or full dict). Loads the dictionary into the context (costly); intended for one-off use.
requirements: ctx must be a valid CCtx.
dst must be large enough; use ZSTD_compressBound().
dict is used if dict != NULL and dictSize >= 8; otherwise no dictionary is used.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress_usingDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress_usingDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const void* dict, size_t dictSize)
functions.description: One-shot decompression using a known dictionary buffer identical to the one used for compression. Loads the dictionary (costly); intended for one-off use.
requirements: dctx must be a valid DCtx.
dstCapacity must be an upper bound on decompressed size.
dict must be identical to the compression dictionary when one was used; if dict == NULL or dictSize < 8, no dictionary is used.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_createCDict
functions.signature: ZSTD_CDict* ZSTD_createCDict(const void* dictBuffer, size_t dictSize, int compressionLevel)
functions.description: Digests a dictionary buffer into a reusable compression dictionary (CDict). Can be shared across threads. dictBuffer content is copied; buffer can be freed after creation.
requirements: dictBuffer must be readable for dictSize bytes; may be empty (then only the level is carried).
Free with ZSTD_freeCDict().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeCDict
functions.description: Frees a ZSTD_CDict created by ZSTD_createCDict(). Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: CDict may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_compress_usingCDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_compress_usingCDict(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const ZSTD_CDict* cdict)
functions.description: Compresses using a pre-digested dictionary (CDict). Compression level and certain frame parameters are decided at CDict creation (dictID=yes, contentSize=yes, checksum=no).
requirements: cctx must be valid; cdict must be a valid prepared dictionary (non-NULL).
dst must be large enough; use ZSTD_compressBound().
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_createDDict
functions.signature: ZSTD_DDict* ZSTD_createDDict(const void* dictBuffer, size_t dictSize)
functions.description: Digests a dictionary buffer into a reusable decompression dictionary (DDict). dictBuffer is copied; buffer can be freed after creation.
requirements: dictBuffer must be readable for dictSize bytes.
Free with ZSTD_freeDDict().

functions.name: ZSTD_freeDDict
functions.description: Frees a ZSTD_DDict created by ZSTD_createDDict(). Accepts NULL. Returns 0 or an error code.
requirements: ddict may be NULL.
Caller should check return value with ZSTD_isError() if non-zero.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_decompress_usingDDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize, const ZSTD_DDict* ddict)
functions.description: Decompresses using a pre-digested dictionary (DDict). Recommended when reusing the same dictionary multiple times.
requirements: dctx must be valid; ddict must be a valid prepared dictionary (non-NULL).
dstCapacity must be an upper bound on decompressed size.
Return is size or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromDict
functions.signature: unsigned ZSTD_getDictID_fromDict(const void* dict, size_t dictSize)
functions.description: Returns the dictID stored inside a dictionary buffer. Returns 0 if the dictionary is not a conformant zstd dictionary; such dictionaries can still be used as content-only dictionaries.
requirements: dict must be readable for dictSize bytes.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromCDict
functions.description: Returns the dictID of the dictionary loaded into a CDict, or 0 if non-conformant or empty.
requirements: cdict must be a valid pointer to a ZSTD_CDict.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromDDict
functions.description: Returns the dictID of the dictionary loaded into a DDict, or 0 if non-conformant or empty.
requirements: ddict must be a valid pointer to a ZSTD_DDict.

functions.name: ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame
functions.signature: unsigned ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame(const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: Extracts the dictID required to decompress the frame at src, if present. Returns 0 if no dictID could be decoded or not needed, frame header too small, or not a zstd frame.
requirements: src should point to the start of a frame; srcSize should be at least the frame header size (ideally >= ZSTD_FRAMEHEADERSIZE_MAX for reliable parsing).
For detailed error causes use ZSTD_getFrameHeader() in static API.

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_loadDictionary(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const void* dict, size_t dictSize)
functions.description: Builds and loads an internal compression dictionary into the CCtx. Sticky: applies to future frames until cleared. Loading builds tables and prevents changing compression parameters afterwards.
requirements: cctx must be valid.
dict may be NULL or size 0 to clear the dictionary (return to no-dictionary mode).
After loading, compression parameters can no longer be changed until reset.
dict content is copied internally; caller may free buffer.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_refCDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_refCDict(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const ZSTD_CDict* cdict)
functions.description: References an existing prepared CDict for all next compressed frames. CDict parameters supersede CCtx parameters labeled as superseded-by-cdict.
requirements: cctx must be valid.
cdict may be NULL to clear and return to no-dictionary mode; otherwise it must outlive its use in cctx.
Only one dictionary can be referenced at a time; referencing a new one discards the previous.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_CCtx_refPrefix
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_CCtx_refPrefix(ZSTD_CCtx* cctx, const void* prefix, size_t prefixSize)
functions.description: References a single-use raw prefix for the next compressed frame. Tables are discarded at end of frame. Faster diff-like compression for similar data.
requirements: cctx must be valid.
Referencing any prefix (including NULL) invalidates any previous prefix or dictionary.
prefix buffer is referenced (not copied) and must outlive the compression and remain unmodified during compression.
Ensure window size is large enough if matching against large sources (see ZSTD_c_windowLog).
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_loadDictionary(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const void* dict, size_t dictSize)
functions.description: Builds and loads an internal decompression dictionary into the DCtx. Sticky: used for future frames until cleared.
requirements: dctx must be valid.
dict may be NULL or size 0 to clear the dictionary.
dict content is copied internally; caller may free buffer after loading.
Loading builds tables and has non-negligible CPU/latency cost; prefer load-once, reuse-many.
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_refDDict
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_refDDict(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const ZSTD_DDict* ddict)
functions.description: References a prepared DDict for decompressing next frames. Sticky until changed/cleared.
requirements: dctx must be valid.
ddict may be NULL to clear and return to no-dictionary mode; otherwise it must outlive its use in dctx.
Only one dictionary can be referenced at a time (unless using experimental multi-dict mode).
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_DCtx_refPrefix
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_DCtx_refPrefix(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, const void* prefix, size_t prefixSize)
functions.description: References a single-use raw prefix for decompressing the next frame; must match the prefix used during compression. Discarded at frame end.
requirements: dctx must be valid.
Referencing any prefix (including NULL) invalidates any previously set prefix or dictionary.
prefix buffer is referenced (not copied) and must outlive decompression and remain unmodified until the frame ends (ZSTD_decompressStream returns 0).
Return 0 or error; check with ZSTD_isError().

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_CCtx
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the compression context object. May vary over time.
requirements: cctx must be a valid pointer or NULL? (Header does not state NULL acceptance; pass a valid CCtx).

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_DCtx
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the decompression context object. May vary over time.
requirements: dctx must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_CStream
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the streaming compression object. May vary over time.
requirements: zcs must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_DStream
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the streaming decompression object. May vary over time.
requirements: zds must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_CDict
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the CDict object.
requirements: cdict must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ZSTD_sizeof_DDict
functions.description: Returns the current memory usage of the DDict object.
requirements: ddict must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: ZSTD_readSkippableFrame
functions.signature: size_t ZSTD_readSkippableFrame(void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, unsigned* magicVariant, const void* src, size_t srcSize)
functions.description: If src starts with a skippable frame, copies its payload into dst and returns bytes written. Writes the magic variant (0..15) to magicVariant if non-NULL. Returns error if not skippable or dst too small.
requirements: src must contain an entire skippable frame; srcSize must be at least the frame size including header.
dst must be large enough to hold the payload; otherwise returns an error.

import random
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid and interesting arbitrary binary blobs suitable
# for Zstandard fuzzing stubs that expect FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME inputs.
# Strategy:
# - Generate small-to-medium sized buffers (0..1024 bytes, capped by harness) with
#   varied, but valid contents that exercise compression paths: highly compressible
#   runs, repetitive patterns with different periods, structured headers, random data,
#   dictionary-like ASCII, Unicode-like sequences, and mixtures.
# - Randomly choose among several templates and combine segments to create variety
#   while keeping data valid (no malformed constraints since arbitrary binary is allowed).
# - Keep overall size <= 1024 bytes to align with harness caps, and far below 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 1024

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getbits(8) if hasattr(rng, 'getbits') else rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _highly_compressible(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    # Long runs with small variations
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    while remaining > 0:
        run_len = min(remaining, rng.randint(8, 128))
        b = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        # Occasionally create a tiny gradient to make RLE and matchers work
        if rng.random() < 0.3 and run_len >= 16:
            base = b
            grad = bytes(((base + (i % 3)) & 0xFF) for i in range(run_len))
            chunks.append(grad)
        else:
            chunks.append(bytes([b]) * run_len)
        remaining -= run_len
    return b"".join(chunks)

def _periodic_pattern(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    period = rng.choice([2,3,4,5,7,8,16,32,64])
    token = _rand_bytes(rng, min(period, max(1, n)))
    rep = (n + len(token) - 1) // len(token)
    data = (token * rep)[:n]
    # Optionally insert small mutations while keeping repetition dominant
    if n >= 16 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        m = rng.randint(1, max(1, n // 32))
        ba = bytearray(data)
        for _ in range(m):
            idx = rng.randrange(0, n)
            ba[idx] ^= rng.randrange(1, 256)
        data = bytes(ba)
    return data

def _structured_like(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Craft data that looks like common file headers to explore dictionary/heuristics.
    # We'll not exceed n and keep arbitrary binary validity.
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    headers = [
        b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",           # PNG
        b"PK\x03\x04",                   # ZIP local header
        b"%PDF-1." + bytes([rng.randrange(48, 58)]), # PDF
        b"\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x03", # GZIP header
        b"OggS\x00\x02\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00",
        b"SQLite format 3\x00",
        b"{\"k\":\"v\"}",
    ]
    hdr = rng.choice(headers)
    take = min(len(hdr), remaining)
    parts.append(hdr[:take])
    remaining -= take
    # Follow with blocks of ascii, numbers, and random tail
    while remaining > 0:
        kind = rng.randrange(3)
        if kind == 0:
            block = (b"A" * rng.randint(1, min(64, remaining))) + (b"0" * rng.randint(0, min(32, max(0, remaining - 1))))
        elif kind == 1:
            text = (
                b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. "
                b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. "
            )
            rep = rng.randint(1, 8)
            # Choose an upper bound >= lower bound to avoid empty range
            upper = min(remaining, 256)
            lower = 1 if upper >= 1 else 0
            length = rng.randint(lower, upper) if upper >= lower and upper > 0 else remaining
            block = (text * rep)[:length]
        else:
            upper = min(remaining, 128)
            length = rng.randint(1, upper) if upper >= 1 else 0
            block = _rand_bytes(rng, length)
        block = block[:remaining]
        parts.append(block)
        remaining -= len(block)
    return b"".join(parts)

def _unicode_like(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # UTF-8-like sequences with valid codepoints mixed with ASCII
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    out = bytearray()
    def emit(b: bytes):
        nonlocal out
        take = min(len(b), max(0, n - len(out)))
        out.extend(b[:take])
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        remain = n - len(out)
        if choice < 0.5 or remain == 1:
            emit(bytes([rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F)]))
        elif choice < 0.7 and remain >= 2:
            # 2-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x7FF)
            emit(bytes([0xC0 | (cp >> 6), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)]))
        elif choice < 0.9 and remain >= 3:
            # 3-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x800, 0xFFFF)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0xE000 + (cp - 0xD800)  # avoid surrogates
            emit(bytes([0xE0 | (cp >> 12), 0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)]))
        elif remain >= 4:
            # 4-byte
            cp = rng.randrange(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)
            emit(bytes([
                0xF0 | (cp >> 18),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
                0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
            ]))
        else:
            # Fallback single byte if not enough space
            emit(bytes([rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F)]))
    return bytes(out)

def _dictionary_like(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    # Mix of tokens, small words, repeated keys; useful for dict/prefix references
    words = [
        b"id", b"name", b"value", b"type", b"meta", b"data", b"timestamp",
        b"header", b"payload", b"count", b"status", b"index", b"offset",
    ]
    separators = [b":", b"=", b" ", b",", b";", b"\n"]
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        k = rng.choice(words)
        # Ensure we don't overshoot remaining excessively
        remain = n - len(out)
        v_len_max = min(32, max(0, remain - len(k) - 1))
        v_len = rng.randint(0, v_len_max) if v_len_max > 0 else 0
        v = _highly_compressible(rng, v_len) if rng.random() < 0.5 else _rand_bytes(rng, v_len)
        pair = k + rng.choice(separators) + v
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            pair += rng.choice(separators)
        take = min(len(pair), n - len(out))
        out.extend(pair[:take])
        if take == 0:
            break
    return bytes(out)

def _mixed(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    if n <= 0:
        return b""
    # Combine several segments from the above generators
    gens = [_highly_compressible, _periodic_pattern, _structured_like, _unicode_like, _dictionary_like]
    rng.shuffle(gens)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    for g in gens:
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        # Allocate a variable portion for each part
        part_len = rng.randint(0, remaining)
        if part_len == 0:
            continue
        parts.append(g(rng, part_len))
        remaining -= part_len
    if remaining > 0:
        parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, remaining))
    return b"".join(parts)

TEMPLATES = [
    _highly_compressible,
    _periodic_pattern,
    _structured_like,
    _unicode_like,
    _dictionary_like,
    _mixed,
]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose overall size within harness-friendly range
    # Favor small and mid sizes with occasional larger payloads
    size_choice = rng.random()
    if size_choice < 0.15:
        total = rng.randint(0, 32)
    elif size_choice < 0.7:
        total = rng.randint(33, 256)
    elif size_choice < 0.95:
        total = rng.randint(257, 768)
    else:
        total = rng.randint(769, MAX_TOTAL)
    total = min(total, MAX_TOTAL)

    # Build data from one or more templates
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Single template
        tmpl = rng.choice(TEMPLATES)
        data = tmpl(rng, total)
    else:
        # Multi-segment composition for diversity
        segments = rng.randint(2, 5)
        lengths = []
        remaining = total
        for _ in range(segments - 1):
            if remaining <= 0:
                lengths.append(0)
                continue
            l = rng.randint(0, remaining)
            lengths.append(l)
            remaining -= l
        lengths.append(max(0, remaining))
        rng.shuffle(lengths)
        data_parts: List[bytes] = []
        for l in lengths:
            if l == 0:
                continue
            tmpl = rng.choice(TEMPLATES)
            data_parts.append(tmpl(rng, l))
        data = b"".join(data_parts)
        # Ensure exact size
        if len(data) < total:
            data += _rand_bytes(rng, total - len(data))
        elif len(data) > total:
            data = data[:total]

    # Final clamp just in case
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data

import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for arbitrary Zstandard dictionary buffers.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid and interesting dictionary-like byte sequences.
# - Sometimes emit conformant zstd dictionary headers with dictID and trainer parameters.
# - Sometimes emit raw content-only dictionaries (any bytes, including empty).
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic randomness via provided seed.

# Zstd dictionary formats (simplified for generator purposes):
# - Content-only dict: arbitrary bytes, may be empty; usable by APIs even if not conformant.
# - Conformant dictionary: magic number 0xEC30A437 (little endian), followed by metadata blocks
#   including an optional dictID. We will craft a minimal plausible header + payload that many
#   parsers accept for dictID extraction and usage. We keep fields conservative to avoid errors.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII text, zeros, and random bytes to get compressible and incompressible regions
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = n
    while remaining > 0:
        mode = rng.randrange(4)
        if mode == 0:
            # ASCII words
            words = [b"lorem", b"ipsum", b"dolor", b"sit", b"amet", b"zstd", b"dictionary", b"prefix", b"compress", b"decompress"]
            w = rng.choice(words)
            rep = rng.randint(1, 16)
            chunk = (w + b" ") * rep
        elif mode == 1:
            # Zero run
            chunk = b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 64)
        elif mode == 2:
            # Repeated pattern
            p = rng.randbytes(1)
            chunk = p * rng.randint(1, 128)
        else:
            # Random bytes
            chunk = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(1, 128))
        if len(chunk) > remaining:
            chunk = chunk[:remaining]
        chunks.append(chunk)
        remaining -= len(chunk)
    return b"".join(chunks)


def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _make_conformant_dict(rng: random.Random, payload_size: int, include_id: bool) -> bytes:
    # Construct a minimal dictionary blob compliant with zstd dictionary format v0. Dict layout:
    # magic (4) = 0xEC30A437 (little endian), followed by fields. We will build a minimal valid
    # header per public zstd doc: [magic][dictID (optional)][reserved/params][content].
    # To keep it broadly acceptable, we place:
    # - magic
    # - dictID field as: 0x01 tag + 4-byte dictID (this is a simplification; many tools accept it)
    # - a simple parameters block tag 0x04 with small windowLog etc., very conservative
    # - payload bytes
    # - footer with checksum tag 0x06 + crc32 of payload (optional)
    # Note: Even if not perfectly matching latest spec nuances, it should be accepted by
    # ZSTD_getDictID_fromDict() in many cases and still usable as content-only if ignored.

    magic = struct.pack('<I', 0xEC30A437)
    parts: List[bytes] = [magic]

    if include_id:
        dict_id = rng.getrandbits(32)
        # tag 0x01 (Dictionary ID), 4 bytes
        parts.append(b"\x01")
        parts.append(struct.pack('<I', dict_id))

    # Very small parameters block: tag 0x04, then 3 bytes for windowLog(18), dictContentType(raw=0), checksumFlag(0)
    parts.append(b"\x04")
    params = bytes([18, 0, 0])
    parts.append(params)

    # Payload tag 0x02, length (varint). We'll encode length as 2-byte little-endian then data.
    # Using a simple fixed-width encoding here: [0x02][len_le16][payload]
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, payload_size)
    parts.append(b"\x02")
    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', len(payload)))
    parts.append(payload)

    # Optional checksum tag 0x06
    parts.append(b"\x06")
    parts.append(struct.pack('<I', _crc32(payload)))

    return b"".join(parts)


def _make_content_only_dict(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    return _rand_bytes(rng, size)


def _maybe_empty(rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    # Occasionally return an empty dictionary to exercise no-dict paths.
    return rng.random() < 0.08


def _biased_sizes(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Choose sizes that hit common fuzzer bounds in stubs (<=512 or <=1024), as well as tiny and medium.
    choices: List[Tuple[int, float]] = [
        (0, 0.08),
        (7, 0.06),   # just below 8 (ignored by usingDict APIs)
        (8, 0.10),   # minimum to be considered as dict by some APIs
        (16, 0.10),
        (64, 0.12),
        (128, 0.12),
        (256, 0.12),
        (512, 0.12),
        (1024, 0.10),
        (2048, 0.06),
        (3072, 0.06),
    ]
    r = rng.random()
    acc = 0.0
    for size, p in choices:
        acc += p
        if r <= acc:
            return size
    # Fallback random size up to 3.5KB
    return rng.randint(1, 3584)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide dictionary style
    style = rng.choices(
        population=["content", "conformant_no_id", "conformant_with_id"],
        weights=[0.55, 0.20, 0.25],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    if _maybe_empty(rng):
        return b""  # Exercise empty/clear-dictionary paths

    target_size = min(_biased_sizes(rng), _MAX_SIZE)

    if style == "content":
        return _make_content_only_dict(rng, target_size)

    # Conformant styles: keep payload a bit smaller to leave room for headers
    payload_size = max(1, min(target_size - 16, 1024))
    include_id = (style == "conformant_with_id")
    blob = _make_conformant_dict(rng, payload_size, include_id)

    # Clamp to max size if needed
    if len(blob) > _MAX_SIZE:
        blob = blob[:_MAX_SIZE]
    return blob
